<findings>

[observation] [info] 20 entry points — wide API surface, consider consolidating exports
[observation] [info] High cohesion (1) — files are tightly interconnected
[anti-pattern] [warning] "packages/lang-kit/src/index.ts" is production code imported only by tests (6 importer(s), all test files) — either it is dead or its real caller is missing
[anti-pattern] [warning] The foundation tier contains language-specific modules (terraform.ts, sql-references.ts, java-maven-build.ts, gradle-catalog.ts, python-setup-py.ts and others) that duplicate the area owned by the matching lang-* packs. Changing how one language is analysed can therefore mean editing both lang-kit and the pack, which defeats loading packs independently. Move what only one pack needs into that pack, and keep lang-kit to the contract, the registry and facts shared across languages.
[anti-pattern] [info] The lightweight parsers (toml-lite, xml-lite, ini-lite, yaml-subset) sit in the same flat src/ as the pack contract (pack-contract.ts, registry.ts). Group them under src/parsers/ so the contract surface is easy to tell apart from the parsing utilities.
[suggestion] [info] Pin the zone id to 'lang-kit' in .n-dx.json, and pin go-language-pack and java-language-pack to lang-go and lang-java. Every pack-tier zone id would then match its package directory, and ndx zone lookups would be predictable from the path.

</findings>

<insights>

- High cohesion (1) — files are tightly interconnected
- 20 entry points — wide API surface, consider consolidating exports
- High cohesion (1) — files are tightly interconnected
- 20 entry points — wide API surface, consider consolidating exports
- Runtime pack discovery via registry (registry.ts) allows sourcevision to load language analyzers dynamically without hard-coded imports
- Build-file abstractions (build-file.ts, build-model.ts) normalize disparate toolchain formats (Maven, Gradle, go.mod, package.json, pyproject.toml)
- Language facts model (go.ts, java.ts, python.ts, typescript.ts) decouples language-specific knowledge from general file classification
- "packages/lang-kit/src/index.ts" is production code imported only by tests (6 importer(s), all test files) — either it is dead or its real caller is missing
- lang-kit/src holds semantics for specific languages (terraform.ts, sql-references.ts, iac-kinds.ts, go-build.ts, java-maven-build.ts, java-gradle-build.ts, python-setup-py.ts and others) even though @n-dx/lang-terraform, lang-sql, lang-go, lang-java and lang-python packs exist. Knowledge about each language is split between the foundation tier and the runtime-loaded packs.
- lang-kit ships five hand-rolled format parsers (toml-lite, xml-lite, ini-lite, yaml-subset, maven-properties) inside a foundation package with no dependencies. This is general parsing infrastructure, not the pack contract.
- The foundation tier contains language-specific modules (terraform.ts, sql-references.ts, java-maven-build.ts, gradle-catalog.ts, python-setup-py.ts and others) that duplicate the area owned by the matching lang-* packs. Changing how one language is analysed can therefore mean editing both lang-kit and the pack, which defeats loading packs independently. Move what only one pack needs into that pack, and keep lang-kit to the contract, the registry and facts shared across languages.
- The lightweight parsers (toml-lite, xml-lite, ini-lite, yaml-subset) sit in the same flat src/ as the pack contract (pack-contract.ts, registry.ts). Group them under src/parsers/ so the contract surface is easy to tell apart from the parsing utilities.
- The zone id 'language-pack-foundation' is a descriptive role name, while the package is @n-dx/lang-kit. Sibling zones use package names (lang-runtime, lang-sql, lang-terraform, lang-python), and the Go and Java packs use a third pattern (go-language-pack, java-language-pack). Pack zones therefore follow three naming schemes.
- Pin the zone id to 'lang-kit' in .n-dx.json, and pin go-language-pack and java-language-pack to lang-go and lang-java. Every pack-tier zone id would then match its package directory, and ndx zone lookups would be predictable from the path.
- [call graph] 486 internal calls, 2 outgoing, 200 incoming (cohesion: 1, coupling: 0)

</insights>
